lab.name: Bacteria & Mixed Cultures
lab.description: Souring bacteria and mixed fermentation cultures. These are not yeast — they are lactic and acetic acid bacteria that produce acid rather than (much) alcohol, plus the blended cultures that combine them with Saccharomyces and Brettanomyces. Catalogued at species level, which means most numeric specs are deliberately null: a species does not have a temperature range, a product does. Where a figure appears it comes from a named commercial datasheet for a specific product, and that product is named in the entry.

attribution: Every numeric field in this file traces to one of three named documents, recorded per strain in specBasis/sourceTitle/sourceUrl: the Lallemand WildBrew Sour Pitch technical data sheet (vendor spec for a specific product); Vriesekoop et al. 2012, '125th Anniversary Review: Bacteria in brewing: the good, the bad and the ugly', Journal of the Institute of Brewing 118:335-345 (peer-reviewed); and the Maltose Falcons homebrew club's 'Brewing Sour and Wild Ales' (club guide). Qualitative behaviour is attributed the same way. Fields no source supports are null rather than estimated.

strains.name: Lactobacillus plantarum
strains.description: The workhorse of kettle souring. Lallemand's WildBrew Sour Pitch is a L. plantarum product and its datasheet is the source of the figures here: 30-40 °C, reaching pH 3.2-3.5, pitched at 10 g/hL. The datasheet classifies it as a facultative hetero-fermentative strain and specifies unhopped wort. Produces little alcohol itself.
strains.flavorNotes: Citrus, tangy, sour (WildBrew Sour Pitch datasheet descriptors).
strains.optimalPitchNote: The datasheet's temperature range is given for unhopped wort, so sour before any hop addition. The recommended dose is 10 g/hL and the product is specified at >10^11 CFU/g. This entry deliberately states no IBU inhibition threshold: an earlier version of this record claimed '5-8 IBU', which the datasheet does not say and which was not sourced.
strains.sourceTitle: Lallemand WildBrew Sour Pitch — Technical Data Sheet
strains.sourceNote: Supports: species, 30-40 °C, pH 3.2-3.5, 10 g/hL, >10^11 CFU/g, flavour descriptors, style list, unhopped-wort requirement. Does not support: attenuation, alcohol tolerance, flocculation, or any IBU threshold — all null.

strains.name: Lactobacillus brevis
strains.description: The most hop-tolerant of the common lactic acid bacteria, and for that reason the classic beer-spoilage organism as well as a deliberate souring culture for long mixed-culture ageing rather than quick kettle souring. Vriesekoop et al.'s review identifies it as among the most hop-resistant and most commonly implicated beer-spoilage LAB; hop iso-alpha-acids act as ionophores that collapse the proton motive force, and hop resistance is what lets L. brevis survive them.
strains.flavorNotes: Lactic acidity. This entry no longer claims a specific funk development curve, which was unsourced.
strains.optimalPitchNote: A genuine spoilage risk in clean beer — segregate soft equipment (tubing, gaskets, buckets). No temperature, alcohol-tolerance or IBU figures are given here: the cited review establishes relative hop resistance qualitatively but does not publish a species-wide numeric range, and strain variation is large.
strains.sourceTitle: Vriesekoop et al. (2012), 125th Anniversary Review: Bacteria in brewing — the good, the bad and the ugly, J. Inst. Brew. 118:335-345
strains.sourceNote: Supports: relative hop tolerance, spoilage significance, mechanism of hop inhibition. Does not support: any temperature range, alcohol tolerance, attenuation or IBU threshold — all null. Previous version asserted 20-35 °C, 8% ABV and '10-15 IBU' with no source.

strains.name: Pediococcus damnosus
strains.description: The slow, deep souring organism of traditional Belgian sour beer, and with L. brevis one of the two lactic acid bacteria most often responsible for beer spoilage. The Maltose Falcons' club guide describes its working behaviour: it produces large amounts of lactic acid from glucose, produces no CO2, and the early stages of the ferment carry a massive charge of diacetyl.
strains.flavorNotes: Deep lactic sourness; heavy diacetyl (butterscotch) during the process, per the Maltose Falcons guide.
strains.optimalPitchNote: Expect a ropy phase and heavy diacetyl early on. Both are described as normal stages by the club guide, which pairs Pediococcus with Brettanomyces so the Brett cleans up what the Pedio leaves. Do not dump it on the strength of the ropy phase. No temperature or alcohol-tolerance figures are asserted — neither cited source publishes them for this species.
strains.sourceTitle: Maltose Falcons Homebrew Club — Brewing Sour and Wild Ales (Pediococcus section); hop-tolerance and spoilage context from Vriesekoop et al. 2012, J. Inst. Brew. 118:335-345
strains.sourceNote: Supports: lactic from glucose, no CO2 production, massive early diacetyl charge, Brett pairing. Does not support: temperature range, alcohol tolerance, attenuation — all null. Previous version asserted 16-29 °C and 10% ABV with no source.

strains.name: Acetobacter
strains.description: The 'vinegar mother'. It converts ethanol into acetic acid, which is what makes vinegar, and it needs oxygen to do it — that oxygen dependence is the whole control lever. In a sealed, topped-up vessel it does very little; in a barrel with headspace or a leaking bung it takes over.
strains.flavorNotes: Vinegar, sharp acetic bite. This entry no longer quantifies an ethyl acetate threshold, which was unsourced.
strains.optimalPitchNote: Almost never pitched deliberately in beer. Control it by controlling oxygen: keep vessels full and sealed. No temperature range is given — the cited sources describe the organism's role and oxygen requirement but publish no range.
strains.sourceTitle: Maltose Falcons Homebrew Club — Brewing Sour and Wild Ales ('Acetobacter — Vinegar Mother — converts ethanol to acetic acid'); brewing-spoilage context from Vriesekoop et al. 2012, J. Inst. Brew. 118:335-345
strains.sourceNote: Supports: ethanol-to-acetic-acid conversion, role as spoilage/complexity organism. Does not support: temperature range — null. Previous version asserted 16-32 °C with no source.

strains.name: Lambic / Mixed-Culture Blend (generic)
strains.description: The traditional consortium, sold commercially as blends — the Maltose Falcons' guide names White Labs WLP655 Belgian Sour Mix, Wyeast 3278 Belgian Lambic Blend and Wyeast 3763 Roeselare Blend. Saccharomyces ferments the sugars first, Lactobacillus and Pediococcus acidify, and Brettanomyces works slowly on what the others leave behind.
strains.flavorNotes: Barnyard funk, lactic tartness, leather. Character development is slow — see the timeline below.
strains.optimalPitchNote: The club guide's own timeline: expect at least a month before the cultures show any character at all, and optimally six months to a year to let the beer bloom. Use dedicated soft equipment and keep this culture away from clean beer. This entry no longer claims a '1-3 year, three-for-gueuze' schedule or a specific 1.000 finishing gravity — those figures were not sourced.
strains.sourceTitle: Maltose Falcons Homebrew Club — Brewing Sour and Wild Ales (incl. 'The Falcon Method For Fermenting Lambics', credited to MB Raines)
strains.sourceNote: Supports: the consortium's composition and division of labour, the named commercial blends, and the 'at least a month / six months to a year' timeline. Does not support: attenuation, temperature, alcohol tolerance, terminal gravity — all null.

strains.name: Lactobacillus delbrueckii
strains.description: Produces lactic acid for a crisp, dry acidity and is the primary souring character of Berliner Weisse. The Maltose Falcons' guide gives the one figure recorded here: ferment it very warm, on the order of 98 °F (37 °C).
strains.optimalPitchNote: The cited guide gives a single warm target (~98 °F) rather than a range, so only the minimum is populated here and the maximum is null. Do not read the 98 °F figure as an upper limit.
strains.sourceTitle: Maltose Falcons Homebrew Club — Brewing Sour and Wild Ales (Lactobacillus section)
strains.sourceNote: Supports: lactic acid production, crisp dry acidity, primary character of Berliner Weisse, warm ferment ~98 °F. Does not support: an upper temperature bound, alcohol tolerance, attenuation — all null.

strains.name: Brettanomyces lambicus
strains.description: The Brett of lambic — the Maltose Falcons' guide associates it with 'every lambic' and describes it as the biggest Brett character of the three commonly used species.
strains.flavorNotes: Huge 'horsey' Brett character with some fruitiness, plus smoky and sour flavours (Maltose Falcons descriptors).
strains.optimalPitchNote: Slow. Numeric specs are null: the cited guide characterises the species by flavour and origin, not by temperature, attenuation or alcohol tolerance, and those vary by isolate. An earlier version of this record described it as a 'cherry-pie Brett' with 85-100% attenuation and 12% tolerance; the cherry framing and all three numbers were unsourced.
strains.sourceTitle: Maltose Falcons Homebrew Club — Brewing Sour and Wild Ales (Brettanomyces section)
strains.sourceNote: Supports: association with lambic, 'horsey' character with fruitiness, smoky and sour notes. Does not support: attenuation, temperature, flocculation, alcohol tolerance — all null.

strains.name: Brettanomyces claussenii
strains.description: The softest of the commonly used Brett species. The Maltose Falcons' guide gives its origin as English stock beer and calls it a softer Brett — a reasonable first Brett for that reason.
strains.flavorNotes: Pineapple and mango; soft rather than barnyard (Maltose Falcons descriptors).
strains.optimalPitchNote: Numeric specs are null — the cited guide describes origin and aroma contribution only. Attenuation and alcohol tolerance figures in an earlier version of this record were unsourced.
strains.sourceTitle: Maltose Falcons Homebrew Club — Brewing Sour and Wild Ales (Brettanomyces section)
strains.sourceNote: Supports: English stock beer origin, softer Brett character, pineapple/mango aroma. Does not support: attenuation, temperature, flocculation, alcohol tolerance — all null.

strains.name: Brettanomyces anomalus
strains.description: Treated by the Maltose Falcons' guide as closely related to B. claussenii, sharing its softer character rather than the lambic strains' funk.
strains.flavorNotes: Soft, fruity — pineapple and mango, as for the related B. claussenii (Maltose Falcons).
strains.optimalPitchNote: Numeric specs are null. An earlier version of this record placed it 'between claussenii's fruit and bruxellensis's funk' with spicy and floral notes and a full set of numbers; none of that was sourced, and the cited guide in fact groups it with claussenii.
strains.sourceTitle: Maltose Falcons Homebrew Club — Brewing Sour and Wild Ales (Brettanomyces section)
strains.sourceNote: Supports: relation to B. claussenii and the shared softer/fruity character. Does not support: attenuation, temperature, flocculation, alcohol tolerance, or a distinct 'spicy/floral' profile — all removed or null.
